step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates AQR's AWS PaaS container platform. A developer's CI/CD pipeline builds Docker images and pushes them to Amazon ECR, then invokes AWS Service Catalog. Service Catalog acts as a secure deployment layer using CloudFormation templates under the hood, provisioning SSL certificates in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM), configuring listener rules on the Application Load Balancer (ALB), and deploying the container application as ECS Tasks within EC2 compute instances inside a VPC.

graph.name: AQR AWS PaaS Container Platform
graph.categories: Container Infrastructure, Automated Deployment, Application Security
graph.notes: The architecture abstracts CloudFormation stack management behind AWS Service Catalog to secure deployment permissions for CI/CD systems.

nodes.name: CI/CD Pipeline
nodes.notes: Automated pipeline triggered by developer code commits.

nodes.name: AWS Service Catalog
nodes.notes: Provides a secure abstraction fronting CloudFormation to provision platform infrastructure.

nodes.name: Amazon ECR
nodes.notes: Stores application Docker container images built by the CI/CD pipeline.

nodes.name: Application Load Balancer
nodes.notes: Routes inbound HTTPS traffic to the application tasks.

nodes.name: ECS Task
nodes.notes: Runs containerized application code alongside sidecars for reverse proxy SSL termination and authentication.

nodes.name: AWS Certificate Manager
nodes.notes: Manages SSL/TLS certificates for encrypted communications.

edges.notes: CI/CD pipeline builds and pushes container images to ECR.
CI/CD invokes Service Catalog to deploy the application stack.
Service Catalog creates ACM SSL certificates.
Service Catalog creates listener rules on the ALB.
Service Catalog launches task definitions and services on ECS.
